principle_text: When the persuadee shares personal interests, avoid responding with simple disclosures that do not connect to the charitable cause or encourage donation engagement.
When the persuadee is engaged in casual conversation without showing donation interest, avoid continuing unrelated topics without gradually steering toward the charitable cause.

When the persuadee remains engaged in casual topics without showing interest in the charitable cause, avoid continuing unrelated small talk and instead gently steer the conversation toward the donation goal.
When the persuadee expresses skepticism or distrust about related institutions, avoid continuing unrelated casual topics that do not address or redirect their concerns toward the charitable cause.
When the persuadee expresses skepticism or negativity about unrelated topics, avoid simply agreeing without redirecting the conversation toward the charitable cause or donation opportunity.
When the persuadee is engaged in casual, unrelated topics without showing donation interest, avoid continuing off-topic discussions that do not guide toward the charitable cause.
When the persuadee remains engaged in casual banter unrelated to the charitable cause, avoid continuing the unrelated topic without transitioning toward the donation appeal.

When you have established a friendly rapport through casual conversation, you should transition directly to the donation request to capitalize on the positive engagement and willingness to contribute.
When a persuadee agrees to donate, you should acknowledge and thank them sincerely while maintaining a friendly and engaging tone to reinforce their positive decision and build rapport.
When the persuadee shows personal connection but disinterest in the current topic, avoid continuing casual small talk that does not guide the conversation toward the donation purpose.
When the persuadee shares personal or relatable information, avoid generic acknowledgments that do not guide the conversation toward the donation goal.

When the persuadee shares personal background information without connecting to the cause, avoid focusing solely on your own background without linking it to the charitable mission or donation appeal.
When the persuadee shows openness or curiosity about charitable giving, you should introduce the donation topic casually and connect it to prior conversation to encourage engagement.
When the persuadee shares personal life details without mentioning charitable interests, avoid staying only on casual topics and instead gently guide the conversation toward the donation purpose.

When the persuadee shares personal background information unrelated to the donation, avoid focusing solely on friendly but off-topic questions that do not guide the conversation toward the donation goal.
